T0.scene_summary: A small office with a window and blinds, low cubby shelf, floor lamp, two rolling chairs, a table, a paneled door and a foreground plant.
T0.overall_evidence: Most prominent objects and their broad arrangement are recognizable, but the viewpoint and framing differ noticeably, and the door, floor, furniture colors and several visible details diverge from the reference.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction uses a more elevated, downward-looking composition: more tabletop and floor are visible, the window is cropped at the top, and the chairs and plant occupy different positions in the frame.
main_defects.evidence: The reference shows the full window frame and a large foreground tabletop clipped at the bottom; the reconstruction cuts off the top of the window and shows the table's legs and a broader floor area.
main_defects.uncertainty: Differences in object placement and camera field of view may also contribute to the framing mismatch.

main_defects.description: The reference's dark brown, visibly grained plank floor and dark gray tabletop are replaced by pale, relatively uniform surfaces; the chairs are also much lighter.
main_defects.evidence: Brown wood-like grain and varied plank coloration are prominent in the reference, while the reconstruction floor is light gray with sparse seams and little visible grain. The reference tabletop is charcoal gray versus light gray in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and exposure can affect perceived color, but do not fully account for the missing floor grain.

main_defects.description: The reference door appears partly open and dark, with recessed panels; the reconstruction appears as a pale, flat panel against the wall with protruding-looking rectangular sections.
main_defects.evidence: The reference door has a dark angled top edge and a visible light frame behind it; the reconstruction's light door face is close to parallel with the wall and its panel edges read as raised.
main_defects.uncertainty: The exact door opening angle is difficult to infer from a single view, and shading affects whether panels appear recessed.

main_defects.description: The window and blinds appear substantially taller and more dominant relative to the shelf in the reference, while the reconstructed visible blinds are a shallow band above it.
main_defects.evidence: The reference shows a complete large wood-framed window; the reconstruction shows only a shorter visible portion and lacks a comparably prominent outer frame.
main_defects.uncertainty: Top-of-frame cropping and viewpoint contribute to the apparent size difference, so the underlying window dimensions cannot be determined reliably.

main_defects.description: The reference includes a visible broad teal planter and exposed dark soil, whereas only foliage is visible in the reconstruction's foreground.
main_defects.evidence: The teal curved planter occupies much of the lower-right reference image; the reconstructed plant is cropped before any pot or soil is visible.
main_defects.uncertainty: A planter could exist outside the reconstruction frame; this is a visible-composition difference, not proof of missing geometry.

strengths: The room's basic office arrangement is recognizable, including the window blinds over a low wooden cubby shelf.
Both images show a slender floor lamp at the left, two wheeled shell chairs, a rectangular table, a paneled door on the right wall, and a spiky foreground plant.
The white walls, light wood shelf, and general distribution of furniture are broadly consistent.
T0.uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Single-view perspective, crop, and lighting differences can mimic changes in object placement, size, and materials; hidden geometry cannot be assessed.

T1.scene_summary: A small light-walled office with a blind-covered window, low cubby shelf, floor lamp, desk, two rolling chairs, a paneled door and a foreground plant.
T1.overall_evidence: The main office objects and their broad arrangement are recognizable, including the shelf beneath the window, lamp at left, two chairs, desk and door at right. Fidelity is reduced by the markedly different framing and furniture orientations, the light rather than dark door, and the loss of the reference's wood-grained floor and darker desk surfaces.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction uses a wider, more elevated-looking composition: the window is cropped at the top, the desk occupies the left foreground rather than extending diagonally from the lower center, and the door and chairs appear smaller within the frame.
main_defects.evidence: The full window frame is visible in the reference, while its upper portion is outside the reconstruction image; the reference door reaches much closer to the top and bottom of the image.
main_defects.uncertainty: Camera placement and actual object placement or scale could both contribute to the differences.

main_defects.description: The dark charcoal door is rendered light gray, the textured brown wood floor becomes pale and nearly uniform, and the dark gray desk becomes much lighter.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a near-black paneled door and visibly variegated brown planks; the reconstruction has a pale gray door and light floor with subtle plank outlines.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and exposure may account for some color differences, but the contrast and texture changes are pronounced.

main_defects.description: The chairs present different views of their backs and seats, especially the foreground chair, whose back is seen prominently in the reference but whose front and seat face the camera in the reconstruction. The desk's visible long edges also run in a different direction across the frame.
main_defects.evidence: The reference foreground chair shows a broad dark back surface; the reconstruction foreground chair shows a light inner seat and back surface.
main_defects.uncertainty: A changed camera angle could contribute to the apparent orientation differences.

main_defects.description: The window and shelf have a smaller apparent width relative to the door and room in the reconstruction; the door also looks narrower and more like a shallow panel than the reference's large door.
main_defects.evidence: The reference window and shelf each occupy roughly a quarter to a third of image width, while the reconstruction window and shelf occupy a smaller fraction and sit farther from the image edges.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective and cropping confound direct measurement of object proportions; the door's apparent thinness could also reflect its angle.

main_defects.description: The reference shows a second dark tabletop-like foreground surface and a visible teal plant pot, whereas the reconstruction shows one plain tabletop and crops the pot out of view.
main_defects.evidence: A separate gray surface appears at the bottom center of the reference, and the pot occupies the bottom-right corner; neither is visible in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: The extra surface may be another part of the desk, and both it and the pot could exist outside the reconstruction frame.

strengths: The principal office objects are present and broadly arranged like the reference.
The horizontal window blind, open wooden cubbies, slender floor lamp, two caster chairs, paneled door and spiky foreground plant are recognizable.
The light walls and baseboards preserve the general character of the room.
T1.uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Only the two supplied views are available; differences in camera, lighting and cropping can mimic changes in geometry, positions and materials. Hidden or out-of-frame geometry cannot be assessed.
